questionText: In Stanley Miller's 1953 spark-discharge experiment (simulating Oparin-Haldane's primitive reducing atmosphere), what was the exact gas mixture, temperature, and product observed?
options: CH4, H2, NH3, and Water vapor (H2O) at 800°C with electric discharge; yielded simple amino acids (glycine, alanine, aspartic acid)
CO2, O2, N2, and H2O at 25°C; yielded purines and pyrimidines
CH4, CO2, SO2, and O3 at 8000°C; yielded functional bacteriophages
NH3, HCN, and O2 at 100°C; yielded D-glucose and ATP
explanation: S.L. Miller (1953) created electric discharge in a closed flask containing Methane (CH4), Hydrogen (H2), Ammonia (NH3), and Water vapor (H2O) at 800°C (in a 2:2:1 ratio of CH4:H2:NH3), experimentally proving abiotic synthesis of amino acids (glycine, alanine, aspartic acid).

subject: Zoology
chapter: Rank Booster: Evolution, Hardy-Weinberg & Human Ancestry
questionText: Why does the deleterious sickle-cell allele (Hb^S) persist at a high frequency (up to 15-20%) in central African populations despite Hb^S Hb^S homozygotes suffering severe hemolytic anemia?
options: Heterozygote Advantage (Balancing Selection): heterozygous individuals (Hb^A Hb^S, sickle-cell trait) have mild or no anemia under normal oxygen tension, but their parasitized RBCs sickle and are cleared by the spleen when infected by Plasmodium falciparum, conferring strong resistance against lethal cerebral malaria
Plasmodium falciparum mutates Hb^A into Hb^S inside the bone marrow
Hb^S Hb^S homozygotes have higher fertility than Hb^A Hb^A homozygotes
Genetic drift eliminates the normal Hb^A allele in tropical climates
explanation: In malaria-endemic regions, Hb^A Hb^A homozygotes are susceptible to fatal falciparum malaria, while Hb^S Hb^S homozygotes die of sickle-cell disease. Heterozygotes (Hb^A Hb^S) enjoy higher reproductive fitness than either homozygote (heterozygote advantage / balancing selection), maintaining both alleles in the gene pool.

Examine the evolutionary history of plants and vertebrates through geological eras:
Statement I: Zosterophyllum and Rhynia-type plants were early vascular land plants of the Silurian/Devonian periods.
Statement II: Synapsids (Pelycosaurs -> Therapsids) were the reptilian ancestors of Mammals, whereas Sauropsids gave rise to modern Reptiles, Dinosaurs, and Birds.
Statement III: Coelacanth (Latimeria), caught in South Africa in 1938, is a living fossil lobe-finned fish (Crossopterygii) related to the ancestors of early amphibians.
Which statements are CORRECT?
options: Statements I, II and III are all correct
explanation: All three statements come directly from NCERT Evolution diagrams and text: (I) Zosterophyllum evolved along the lycopod line in the Paleozoic; (II) Early reptiles diverged into Synapsids (-> Pelycosaurs -> Therapsids -> Mammals) and Sauropsids (-> Thecodonts -> Crocodiles, Dinosaurs, Birds); (III) Coelacanth is a lobe-fin fish discovered alive in 1938.

subject: Zoology
chapter: Rank Booster: Evolution, Hardy-Weinberg & Human Ancestry
questionText: How did Hugo de Vries' concept of 'Mutation' (based on his work on Oenothera lamarckiana, evening primrose) differ fundamentally from Charles Darwin's concept of 'Variations'?
options: De Vries stated that mutations are random, directionless, and large single-step changes causing speciation ('Saltation'), whereas Darwinian variations are small, heritable, directional, and gradual
De Vries stated that mutations are small, directional, and slow, whereas Darwin proposed single-step saltation
De Vries supported Lamarck's inheritance of acquired characters via use and disuse of organs
Both Darwin and de Vries agreed that speciation never involves reproductive isolation
explanation: According to NCERT: mutations for de Vries are random and directionless, whereas Darwinian variations are small and directional. Evolution for Darwin was gradual, while de Vries believed mutation caused speciation and hence called it Saltation (single step large mutation).

subject: Zoology
chapter: Rank Booster: Evolution, Hardy-Weinberg & Human Ancestry
questionText: When a small group of individuals emigrates from a parent population to colonize a new, isolated island, its allele frequencies often differ drastically by pure chance from the original population, sometimes leading to the formation of a new species. This evolutionary mechanism is known as:
options: Founder Effect (a special case of Genetic Drift / Sewall Wright Effect)
explanation: When allele frequencies change in a small population purely by chance (random sampling error rather than natural selection), it is called Genetic Drift (Sewall Wright effect). When a small founding sample colonizes a new habitat, the original drifted sample becomes the founders of the new population—termed the Founder Effect.

questionText:
Match the placental mammal with its corresponding Australian Marsupial counterpart that evolved via Convergent Evolution (Adaptive Radiation in parallel):
(A) Wolf — (i) Tasmanian wolf (Thylacine)
(B) Mole — (ii) Marsupial mole
(C) Anteater — (iii) Numbat (Banded anteater)
(D) Bobcat / Ocelot — (iv) Tasmanian tiger cat
(E) Flying squirrel — (v) Sugar glider (Flying phalanger)
options: All five pairs (A)-(i), (B)-(ii), (C)-(iii), (D)-(iv), and (E)-(v) are exact ecomorphological counterparts
Only (A)-(i) and (B)-(ii) are correct; Lemur corresponds to Tasmanian wolf
Sugar glider is a placental mammal whereas Flying squirrel is a marsupial
explanation: From NCERT Figure 7.7: When more than one adaptive radiation appeared to have occurred in an isolated geographical area (representing different habitats), one can call this convergent evolution: Wolf <-> Tasmanian wolf; Mole <-> Marsupial mole; Anteater <-> Numbat; Bobcat <-> Tasmanian tiger cat; Flying squirrel <-> Flying phalanger; Lemur <-> Spotted cuscus.

subject: Zoology
chapter: Rank Booster: Evolution, Hardy-Weinberg & Human Ancestry
questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the five factors known to disturb Hardy-Weinberg genetic equilibrium ($p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$)?
options: Random mating (Panmixia) in a very large population
explanation: The five factors known to affect (disturb) Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium are: (1) Gene migration or gene flow, (2) Genetic drift, (3) Mutation, (4) Genetic recombination, and (5) Natural selection. Random mating (panmixia) in a large population is a REQUIRED condition to MAINTAIN Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, not disturb it!

questionText: Identify the completely CORRECT statement regarding animal phyla and their diagnostic characteristics:

Aschelminthes (Roundworms) are acoelomates with metameric segmentation and a closed circulatory system
Ctenophores (Sea walnuts) reproduce both asexually and sexually, possess cnidoblasts, and exhibit internal fertilization
Hemichordates possess a true mesodermal notochord in their proboscis called the stomochord
explanation: Let's check the traps: (1) Echinodermata have bilateral larvae and pentamerous radial adults, calcareous endoskeleton, and water vascular system (Correct!). (2) Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates without segmentation. (3) Ctenophores reproduce ONLY by sexual means, lack cnidoblasts (have colloblasts), and show external fertilization. questionText: Trace the fascinating life cycle of Petromyzon (Lamprey, Class Cyclostomata): where does it live as an adult, where does it migrate for spawning, and what happens to the adult and its Ammocoete larva?
options: Adults are marine ectoparasites on fishes, but migrate to freshwater rivers for spawning (Anadromous migration); within a few days after spawning, the adults DIE, and their filter-feeding Ammocoete larvae, after metamorphosis, return to the ocean
Adults live in freshwater rivers and migrate to the deep sea to spawn (Catadromous), then return to rivers
Petromyzon has paired fins, placoid scales, and cartilaginous jaws
Development is direct without any larval stage
explanation: Verbatim high-yield NCERT Animal Kingdom fact: Cyclostomes (Petromyzon and Myxine) are marine but migrate for spawning to fresh water (anadromous). After spawning, within a few days, they die. Their larvae (Ammocoete), after metamorphosis, return to the ocean.

In Periplaneta americana (Cockroach), examine the anatomical and physiological statements:

(II) A ring of 6-8 blind tubules called hepatic (gastric) caeca is present at the junction of foregut and midgut, while 100-150 yellow filamentous Malpighian tubules are present at the junction of midgut and hindgut.
(III) In the male reproductive system, the mushroom-shaped gland (utricular gland) is located in the 6th-7th abdominal segments, whereas the phallic (conglobate) gland opens near the gonopore.
Which statements are CORRECT?
explanation: All three statements are exact NCERT Structural Organisation in Animals facts for Periplaneta americana: 13-chambered heart with 12 pairs of alary muscles; 6-8 hepatic caeca at foregut-midgut junction; 100-150 Malpighian tubules at midgut-hindgut junction; mushroom gland in 6th-7th abdominal segments of male (spermatheca in 6th segment of female).

questionText: How does the compound eye of a cockroach produce 'Mosaic Vision', and how many ommatidia are present in each compound eye?
options: Each compound eye consists of about 2000 hexagonal ommatidia; a cockroach receives several separate images of an object (mosaic vision) characterized by MORE sensitivity but LESS resolution, especially adapted for nocturnal vision
Each compound eye has 200 ommatidia giving high resolution and low sensitivity
Simple ocelli form mosaic vision with high resolution during daytime
The crystalline cone secretes rhodopsin into the haemolymph
explanation: With the help of about 2000 hexagonal ommatidia in each eye, a cockroach can receive several images of an object. This kind of vision is known as mosaic vision with MORE sensitivity but LESS resolution, being common during night (hence called nocturnal vision).

subject: Zoology
chapter: Rank Booster: Non-Chordate & Chordate Comparative Zoology
questionText:
In the Indian Bullfrog (Rana tigrina), examine the following statements regarding the circulatory, urogenital, and nervous systems:
(I) It has both a Hepatic Portal System and a Renal Portal System, and its RBCs are nucleated and oval.
(II) In male frogs, 10-12 vasa efferentia arise from the testes, enter the kidneys on their side, and open into Bidder's canal, so the ureter acts as a urinogenital duct.
(III) Frogs have 10 pairs of cranial nerves and 10 pairs of spinal nerves.
Which statements are CORRECT?
options: (I) and (II) only; frogs have 12 pairs of cranial nerves
(II) and (III) only; frogs lack a renal portal system
explanation: All three statements are completely accurate! Unlike amniotes (reptiles, birds, mammals) which have 12 pairs of cranial nerves, anamniotes (fishes and amphibians like frog) have 10 pairs of cranial nerves. Male frogs possess Bidder's canal inside the kidney and a common urinogenital duct, whereas in female frogs the ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca.

Osteichthyes have a terminal mouth, cycloid/ctenoid scales, 4 pairs of gills covered by an operculum, and an air bladder that regulates buoyancy
Chondrichthyes are mostly oviparous with external fertilization, whereas Osteichthyes are mostly viviparous with internal fertilization
explanation: Option 4 is completely inverted! Chondrichthyes have INTERNAL fertilization and many of them are VIVIPAROUS (e.g., Scoliodon, Carcharodon, Trygon), whereas Osteichthyes have mostly EXTERNAL fertilization and are mostly OVIPAROUS with direct development.

Match the animal taxon with its unique anatomical or physiological hallmark:
(A) Porifera (Sycon, Spongilla) — (i) Choanocytes (collar cells) lining the spongocoel and water canal system
(B) Cnidaria (Physalia, Adamsia) — (ii) Metagenesis (alternation between asexual polyp and sexual medusa in Obelia)
(C) Mollusca (Octopus, Loligo) — (iii) Radula (file-like rasping organ for feeding) and Feather-like gills in mantle cavity
(D) Aves (Neophron, Struthio) — (iv) Pneumatic hollow bones, crop & gizzard, and air sacs connected to lungs to supplement respiration
options: All four pairs (A)-(i), (B)-(ii), (C)-(iii), and (D)-(iv) are completely accurate
Porifera possess a water vascular system whereas Echinoderms possess a water canal system
Adamsia exhibits metagenesis whereas Obelia exists only in polyp form
Struthio (Ostrich) is a flightless mammal with solid bones
explanation: Watch the classic NCERT traps: Porifera have a Water CANAL System (Ostia -> Spongocoel -> Osculum lined by choanocytes), whereas Echinoderms have a Water VASCULAR System (Madreporite -> Tube feet). Obelia and Physalia exhibit Metagenesis (Polyp produces Medusa asexually; Medusa produces Polyp sexually), whereas Adamsia (Sea anemone) is exclusively a polyp and Aurelia is a medusa.

subject: Zoology
chapter: Rank Booster: Non-Chordate & Chordate Comparative Zoology
questionText:
Examine the classification of Epithelial and Connective Tissues in animals:
Statement I: Ciliated epithelium is present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes to move particles or mucus in a specific direction.
Statement II: Tendons (which attach skeletal muscles to bones) and Ligaments (which attach one bone to another) are examples of Dense Regular Connective Tissue, whereas dermis of the skin is Dense Irregular Connective Tissue.
Statement III: Cartilage matrix contains chondroitin salts and is avascular, whereas bone matrix is rich in calcium salts and collagen fibers with osteocytes housed in lacunae.
Which statements are CORRECT?
options: Statements I, II and III are all correct
explanation: All three statements are 100% accurate from NCERT Structural Organisation in Animals. Dense regular connective tissue has collagen fibers oriented in parallel bundles (Tendons = Muscle to Bone; Ligaments = Bone to Bone), whereas Dense irregular connective tissue has differently oriented fibers (present in skin dermis).

subject: Zoology
chapter: Rank Booster: Non-Chordate & Chordate Comparative Zoology
questionText: Distinguish between the three types of cell junctions found in animal epithelia and cardiac muscle:
options: Tight junctions (Zonula occludens) stop substances from leaking across a tissue; Adhering junctions (Desmosomes) perform cementing to keep neighboring cells together; Gap junctions facilitate rapid communication by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for transfer of ions and small molecules
Tight junctions transfer ions between cells; Gap junctions prevent leakage across epithelia
Adhering junctions form aqueous channels of connexin proteins
Intercalated discs of cardiac muscle lack gap junctions and adhering junctions
explanation: Tight junctions prevent paracellular leakage across epithelial sheets; Adhering junctions (zonula adherens, desmosomes) mechanically anchor cells together; Gap junctions form hydrophilic channels (connexons) connecting adjacent cytoplasms, enabling cardiac muscle cells (at intercalated discs) to contract as a functional syncytium.

subject: Zoology
questionText: The unique mammalian characteristics are

questionText: During which phase(s) of cell cycle, amount of DNA in a cell remains at 4C level if the initial amount is denoted as 2C?
explanation: In the G\u2081 phase, the initial amount of DNA was 2C. In the S phase, DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles. So the amount of DNA becomes 4C. In the G\u2082 phase, there will be no change in the amount of DNA, so it remains 4C. In M phase, cell division occurs. Before dividing into two daughter cells, the amount of DNA was 4C. After cytokinesis, each daughter cell will have 2C amount of DNA. Thus, in the S phase, 2C becomes 4C and at the end of the M phase, 4C becomes 2C. Hence, the amount of DNA remains at 4C during G\u2082.

explanation: The part starting with the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles constitute the conducting part whereas the alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part of the respiratory system. The conducting part transports the atmospheric air to the alveoli, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies and also brings the air to body temperature. The partial pressures (in mmHg) of oxygen (O\u2082) and carbon dioxide (CO\u2082) at alveoli (the site of diffusion) are 104 and 40 respectively. In the atmosphere, pO\u2082 is 159 mm Hg and pCO\u2082 is 0.3 mm Hg. In deoxygenated blood, pO\u2082 is 40 mmHg and pCO\u2082 is 45 mmHg. This increase in thoracic volume causes an increase in pulmonary volume. It decreases the intra-pulmonary pressure to less than atmospheric pressure which allows the entry of air from outside to the lungs i.e., inspiration.

explanation: Tidal volume is the volume of air inspired or expired during normal respiration. It is approximately 500 mL. questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct?

Blood moves freely from atrium to the ventricle during joint diastole
Increased ventricular pressure causes closing of the semilunar valves
explanation: The Sino-atrial node generates new action potential. With the decline of ventricular pressure, the tricuspid and bicuspid valves are pushed open by the pressure in the atria exerted by the blood which was being emptied into them by the veins. Joint diastole refers to the phase in the cardiac cycle of the heart when both atria and ventricles are relaxed. During joint diastole, blood is poured into the left and right atria. Due to this filling of blood, atrioventricular valves (Bicuspid and Tricuspid valves) open and allow blood to flow from atria to ventricles. During ventricular diastole, the ventricular pressure falls causing the closure of semilunar valves and this prevents the backflow of blood into the ventricles.

questionText: What would be the heart rate of a person if the cardiac output is 5L, blood volume in the ventricles at the end of diastole is 100 mL and at the end of ventricular systole is 50 mL.

So, 5000 ml = 50 ml x Heart rate So, Heart rate = 100 beats per minute.

questionText:
During the muscular contraction which of the following events occur? 
(a) ‘H’ zone disappears 
(b) ‘A’ band widens 
(c) ‘I’ band reduces in width 
(d) Myosin hydrolyzes ATP, releasing the ADP and Pi. 
(e) Z-lines attached to actins are pulled inwards 
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: The correct option is (c) because the length of the A-band is retained. During muscle contraction, the following events occur: (1) The globular head of myosin acts as ATPase and hydrolyses ATP molecule and eventually leads to the formation of cross-bridge. (2) This pulls the actin filament towards the center of the \u2018A-band\u2019. (3) The Z-line attached to these actins are also pulled inwards thereby causing a shortening of the sarcomere. (4) The thin myofilaments move past the thick myofilaments due to which the H-zone narrows. This reduces the length of the I-band but retains the length of the A-band. (5) The myosin then releases ADP+PI and goes back to its relaxed state.

subject: Zoology
questionText: If Adenine makes 30% of the DNA molecule, what will be the percentage of Thymine, Guanine, and Cytosine in it?
explanation: Erwin Chargaff proposed three rules which are termed Chargaff's rules. These rules played an important role in the discovery of the double-helix structure of DNA, they are 1. In any double-stranded DNA, the number of guanine units equals the number of cytosine units whereas the number of adenine units equals the number of thymine units (i.e no of A = no of T and no of C = no of G and vice versa). 2. The sum of purines (A and G) equals that of pyrimidines (C and T). The composition of DNA varies from one species to another. According to the question, the percentage of adenine is 30. Thus, the percentage of thymine will be 30 as per the first rule. The sum of A and T would be 60 %. The remaining % of bases is 40% which has to be divided equally between G and C since no of G= no of C. Thus G=C=20%.

subject: Zoology
questionText: Which one of the following statements about Histones is wrong?

The pH of histones is slightly acidic
explanation: Histones are rich in basic amino acids residue lysine and arginine with charged side chains. The pH of histones is basic.

questionText: If there are 999 bases in an RNA that codes for a protein with 333 amino acids and the base at position 901 is deleted such that the length of the RNA becomes 998 bases how many codons will be altered?
explanation: If deletion occurs at the 901st position then the first 900 bases will be normal. The remaining 99 bases will be altered. 3 bases stand for 1 codon, so, 99 bases = 33 codons will be altered due to deletion of one base at 901 position.

subject: Zoology
questionText: During DNA replication, Okazaki fragments are used to elongate
options: The leading strand away from the replication fork.
The lagging strand away from the replication fork
The leading strand towards the replication fork
The lagging strand towards the replication fork
explanation: Two DNA polymerase molecules work simultaneously at the DNA fork, one on the leading strand and the other on the lagging strand. Each Okazaki fragment is synthesized by DNA polymerase at a lagging strand in a 5' \u2192 3' direction. New Okazaki fragments appear as the replication fork opens further. As the first Okazaki fragment appears away from the replication fork, the direction of elongation would be away from the replication fork.

subject: Zoology
questionText: What is it that forms the basis of DNA Fingerprinting?

subject: Zoology
explanation: Adaptive radiation is the process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and literally radiating to other areas of geography, for example, Darwin's finches. Analogous organs which are not anatomically similar structures though they perform similar functions are a result of convergent evolution, for example, Wings of butterflies and of birds. Homologous organs are anatomically similar structures but perform different functions. According to their needs, are a result of divergent evolution, for example, Bones of forelimbs in man and whale. Evolution by anthropogenic action means evolution due to human interference, for example, Antibiotic-resistant microbes, herbicides resistant varieties, and pesticide-resistant varieties.

subject: Zoology
explanation: Polar seals generally have shorter ears and limbs (extremities) to minimize heat loss. This is with reference to Allen's rule. Kangaroo rats exhibit physiological adaptation. Desert lizard shows behavioural adaptation. They lack the physiological ability to cope-up with extreme temperatures but manage the body temperature by behavioural means. Marine fishes at depth are adapted biochemically to survive in great depths in the ocean.

explanation: Evolution by Anthropogenic action is because of the interference by human beings. Darwin\u2019s Finches of Galapagos islands is an example of natural selection.

questionText: Flippers of Penguins and Dolphins are examples of
explanation: Analogous organs have similar functions but different origins. Flippers of penguins and dolphins have a similar function (helps in swimming). However, Penguin and dolphin are not closely related to each other, and hence their flippers have different origins and are called analogous organs. Analogous organs are the cause of convergent evolution.

explanation: Active immunity is slow and takes time to give its full effective response. Foetus receiving some antibodies from their mother, through the placenta during pregnancy is an example of passive immunity. Active immunity is the immunity in which when the host is exposed to antigens either living or dead, antibodies are produced in the host body. In passive immunity, readymade antibodies are directly given to protect the body against foreign agents.

subject: Zoology
questionText:
Given below are two statements: 
Statement I: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific sequences to cut DNA known as palindromic nucleotide sequences. 
Statement II: Restriction endonucleases cut the DNA strand a little away from the centre of the palindromic site.

Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

explanation: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific sequences to cut DNA known as palindromic nucleotide sequences. However, the restriction enzymes cut the strand of DNA a little away from the centre of the palindrome site, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands.

subject: Zoology
questionText: Which of the following is a correct sequence of steps in a PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)?
explanation: Polymerase chain reaction or PCR consists of the following three steps: i)Denaturation- The two DNA strands of template DNA separate from each other when heated to 92\xb0C. ii) Annealing- The primers anneal to the 3\u2019 end of single strands of DNA. iii)Extension- The primers are extended by DNA polymerase by the addition of nucleotides to form complete strands of DNA. Hence the sequence of steps is denaturation, annealing, extension.

questionText: Plasmid pBR322 has a PstI restriction enzyme site within gene ampR that confers ampicillin resistance. If this enzyme is used for inserting a gene for \u03b2-galactoside production and the recombinant plasmid is inserted in an E.coli strain
options: It will lead to lysis of the host cell
It will be able to produce a novel protein with dual ability
It will not be able to confer ampicillin resistance to the host cell
The transformed cells will have the ability to resist ampicillin as well as produce \u03b2-galactoside
explanation: pBR322 is a commonly used cloning vector. When the gene for \u03b2-galactoside is inserted in the ampicillin resistance gene by using Pst I, the recombinant E.coli will lose ampicillin resistance due to insertional inactivation of the antibiotic resistance gene. The host (recombinant) cell will produce \u03b2-galactoside which is not a novel protein nor does it have the dual ability. The transformed cells cannot resist ampicillin as they have lost ampicillin resistance. A recombinant E. coli is produced and the host cell will not undergo lysis due to the insertion of the \u03b2-galactoside gene.

subject: Zoology
questionText: In gene therapy of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency, the patient requires periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes because:
options: Retroviral vector is introduced into these lymphocytes
Gene isolated from marrow cells producing ADA is introduced into cells at embryonic stages
Lymphocytes from patient\u2019s blood are grown in culture, outside the body
Genetically engineered lymphocytes are not immortal cells.
explanation: In some children ADA deficiency can be cured by bone marrow transplantation; in others it can be treated by enzyme replacement therapy, in which functional ADA is given to the patient by injection. But the problem with both of these approaches is that they are not completely curative. As a first step towards gene therapy, lymphocytes from the blood of the patient are grown in a culture outside the body. A functional ADA cDNA (using a retroviral vector) is then introduced into these lymphocytes, which are subsequently returned to the patient. However, as these cells are not immortal, the patient requires periodic infusion of such genetically engineered lymphocytes.

subject: Zoology
questionText:
Statements related to human insulin are given below: Which statement(s) is/are correct about genetically engineered Insulin? 
(a) Pro-hormone insulin contain extra stretch of C-peptide 
(b) A peptide and B-peptide chains of insulin were produced separately in E. coli, extracted and combined by creating a disulphide bond between them. 
(c) Insulin used for treating Diabetes was extracted from Cattles and Pigs. 
(d) Pro-hormone insulin needs to be processed for converting into a mature and functional hormone. 
(e) Some patients develop allergic reactions to the foreign insulin.
explanation: In mammals, including humans, insulin is synthesised as a pro-hormone which contains an extra stretch called the C peptide. The pro-hormone needs to be processed before it becomes fully mature and functional. However, in case of genetically engineered insulin, there is no C-peptide, hence no proinsulin is formed. Genetically engineered insulin that is used for diabetes is produced using yeast and bacteria, unlike natural insulin which was earlier extracted from pancreas of slaughtered cattle and pigs.

subject: Zoology
questionText: For effective treatment of the disease, early diagnosis and understanding its pathophysiology is very important. Which of the following molecular diagnostic techniques is very useful for early detection?
explanation: ELISA can be used for early detection of infection either by detecting the presence of pathogenic antigen or by detecting the antibodies synthesized against the pathogen. In the hybridization technique, an ssDNA/ssRNA tagged with a radioactive molecule (probe) is allowed to hybridize its complementary DNA in a clone of cells followed by detection using autoradiography. It is used to find a mutated gene. The western blotting technique is used to detect a specific protein molecule among a mixture of proteins. Southern blotting is used to detect a specific DNA sequence in the given sample and can be detected prior to antibody formation. One can detect the presence of pathogenic DNA/RNA.
